cards.text: Solomon, king of Israel, has finished the house of the LORD and his own royal palace. Everything he set his heart on doing for them? DONE. That man finished his WHOLE to-do list, friend, and I've had "organize the sprinkles" on mine since the day I got here.

cards.question: One night, the LORD appears to Solomon. What's the first thing He tells him?
The LORD tells Solomon He has chosen this place for Himself as a house of ___.

cards.text: Then the LORD talks about hard days. What if He closes the sky so there's no rain, or commands the locusts to eat up the land, or sends a plague among His people?

cards.question: When hard days like that come, what does the LORD say His people should do?

answers.text: Offer more sacrifices at the temple
Ask their king to fix it

cards.text: He spells it out. His people who are called by His name humble themselves, pray, seek His face and turn from their wicked ways. That last one is turning AROUND, like realizing you've been driving the wrong way for an hour and actually taking the exit.

cards.question: When His people turn back, the LORD says He will hear from heaven, ___ their sin and ___ their land.

cards.text: And this brand-new temple? The LORD says from now on His eyes will be open and His ears attentive to the prayers offered in this place.

cards.question: The LORD tells Solomon that His eyes and His heart will be at this temple for all time.

cards.text: Now the LORD turns to Solomon himself. If you walk before Me the way your father David walked, doing all I've commanded and keeping My statutes and ordinances. Talk about having to follow your dad's act!

cards.question: If Solomon walks with the LORD like David did, the LORD says He will establish Solomon's royal ___.

cards.text: It's the same covenant the LORD made with David when He said, 'You will never fail to have a man to rule over Israel.'
But then the LORD gives the other side. If you turn away and forsake the statutes and commandments I set before you, and go off to serve and worship other gods...

cards.question: The LORD warns about going off to serve other gods. If that happens, what will He do to Israel?

cards.text: And the temple He set apart for His Name? He'll banish it from His presence and make it an object of scorn among all the peoples, until it's a heap of rubble.

cards.question: People passing by the rubble of the temple will just walk on without saying a word.
Passersby ask why the LORD did this to the land and the temple. What do others answer?

answers.text: They forsook Him for other gods

cards.text: And look who they walked away from: the LORD, the God of their fathers, who brought them out of the land of Egypt. That's a heavy word to end on, friend, and Solomon heard every bit of it.

findings.problem: The opening card has 4 sentences: 'Solomon... royal palace.' / 'Everything he set his heart on doing for them?' / 'DONE.' / 'That man finished his WHOLE to-do list...'. The limit is 3.

rule.text: The opening card can be up to 3 sentences.

findings.problem: The question turns the LORD's conditional into an assumed event and an instruction. 'When hard days like that come' replaces 'If I close the sky...' (7:13). 'What does the LORD say His people should do?' reads as a command, but 7:14 states a condition: 'if My people... humble themselves... then I will hear'.

The card drops the 'if' from 7:14. 'His people who are called by His name humble themselves, pray, seek His face and turn from their wicked ways' is stated as something that happens, not as the condition the text gives.
The story card has 3 sentences: 'He spells it out.' / 'His people who are called...' / 'That last one is turning AROUND...'.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: 'When His people turn back' changes the conditional 'if' of 7:14 into 'when', which presents their turning as certain.
The story card has 3 sentences: 'Now the LORD turns to Solomon himself.' / 'If you walk before Me...' / 'Talk about having to follow your dad's act!'.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: '...make it an object of scorn among all the peoples, until it's a heap of rubble' adds a time link the text doesn't state. In 7:20 the temple is made an object of scorn. In 7:21 the text says 'when this temple has become a heap of rubble'. 'Until' implies the scorn leads up to, or ends at, the rubble.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Card 15 already says the temple will be 'an object of scorn among all the peoples'. That rules out the statement that passersby will 'just walk on without saying a word', so the True/False answer is given away by the setup.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.
